chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Four things are done in vain: friendship bestowed upon one who has no loyalty; kindness shown to one who does not give thanks; knowledge shared with one who does not listen; and a secret entrusted to one who has no capacity to safeguard it.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things that are considered vain or futile in social interactions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these four elements—affection, favor, knowledge, and secrets—as 'vain' (dhiya') when the recipient lacks the capacity to reciprocate or preserve them, reflecting the Shia emphasis on discernment (hikmah) in social interactions. This teaching warns against the spiritual and social waste of investing in those who are ungrateful, inattentive, or untrustworthy, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition of evaluating the 'container' for one's gifts.
